payload.proof_nl:
Let x = m + t, where m = floor(x) ∈ Z and t = frac(x) ∈ [(n-1)/n, 1).
For each k ∈ {1,2,\dots,n}, since km is an integer we have
floor(kx) = floor(km + kt) = km + floor(kt).
Now t < 1 implies kt < k, so floor(kt) ≤ k-1. Also t ≥ (n-1)/n and k ≤ n, hence
kt ≥ k(n-1)/n = k - k/n ≥ k-1,
so floor(kt) ≥ k-1. Therefore floor(kt) = k-1 for every 1 ≤ k ≤ n.
Thus, for every such k,
floor(kx) = km + k - 1,
and in particular floor(nx) = nm + n - 1.
Substituting into the definition of F_n(x),
F_n(x) = floor(nx) - \sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k
= (nm+n-1) - \sum_{k=1}^n (km+k-1)/k
= (nm+n-1) - \sum_{k=1}^n \bigl(m + 1 - 1/k\bigr)
= (nm+n-1) - (nm + n - H_n)
= H_n - 1,
where H_n = \sum_{k=1}^n 1/k.
Hence whenever frac(x) ∈ [(n-1)/n, 1), we have F_n(x) = H_n - 1.
